note.text: A public enterprise is owned or controlled by public authorities under its particular arrangement. It may pursue commercial returns, public-service access or strategic objectives. Public ownership differs from regulating a privately owned firm and from selling shares to private members of the public. A mixed-ownership enterprise combines public and private interests. Public enterprises still use scarce resources and require accountability. Neither public ownership nor a service objective proves efficiency, inefficiency or a need for permanent subsidy in every case.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to distinguish government ownership from regulation and assess commercial and service objectives. Builds on: private and cooperative ownership. Leads to: nationalisation and privatisation as changes in ownership.

sections.heading: Follow the local case
sections.text: An invented local transport enterprise charges fares while serving a route valued for access. A classroom record compares fee income with service costs, without identifying a real operator or current fare. Learners can discuss who meets any gap and whether the service goal is clearly defined. A regulated private operator would represent a different ownership arrangement.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Separate ownership, control, regulation and objectives. Assess service outcomes and resource costs together. A subsidy can fund a specified obligation but does not make its resource cost disappear. Do not infer the ownership of a real Cameroonian enterprise from its familiar name.

questions.prompt: In a fictional public-service enterprise, service costs are {cost} CFA francs and fee revenue {fees}. For this simplified record, calculate the funding gap before any subsidy or other finance.

misconceptions.explain: Fee income covers part of costs; it does not add to the gap.
That is fee revenue, not the uncovered amount.

solution: Gap = stated costs minus stated fee revenue.
